headlines.title: Ground stop lifted: Bay Area airports impacted, what happens next?
headlines.description: A storm expected to bring hazardous winds to the Bay Area and Central Coast hit the region Friday. The National Weather Service is forecasting the storm to bring gusts of up to 40 mph. In addition, massive breaking waves are expected along the coast and flooding in low-lying areas. Here’s a look at the latest storm-related incidents NBC Bay Area is aware of: Caltrans postpones Highway 37 closure A nighttime closure of eastbound Highway 37 from Sears Point at the Solano and Sonoma counties line to Mare Island in Vallejo will be rescheduled at a later date to be determined, Caltrans said citing the wet weather. The closure was originally scheduled to take place Monday. For more information the project, visit 37pave.com. Santa Cruz beaches close due to dangerous high surf Authorities in Santa Cruz will temporarily shut down all city beaches and the Santa Cruz Wharf starting 10 p.m. Friday through 5 a.m. Sunday. A high surf warning has been issued this weekend due to waves potentially reaching 25 to 35 feet along portions of the coast. Highway 4 closure postponed due to storm The planned closure of State Route 4 east of Discovery Bay has been postponed due to a stormy weather forecast, Caltrans officials announced Thursday. The full closure was originally scheduled for Sunday and is now expected to happen on Nov. 22 from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. The roadway is being closed from Tracy Boulevard to the San Joaquin/Contra Costa county line east of Discovery Bay for the Old River Bridge maintenance project, according to Caltrans officials. Local access will be allowed for residents and to local businesses only within the closure area. Potential delays could be up to 30 to 40 minutes. People headed east on State Route 4 will be detoured onto Byron Road, then south onto Mountain House Parkway, then east on Interstate 205, then north onto Tracy Boulevard and from there back onto State Route 4. People heading west will be detoured south on Tracy Boulevard, west on Interstate 205, north on Mountain House Parkway, then northwest onto Byron Road and back onto State Route 4. –Bay City News Multiple crashes reported in Santa Cruz county CHP Santa Cruz said officers have been responding to multiple crashes throughout the county on Friday morning. Authorities asked drivers to reduce their speed, turn on their headlights and avoid sudden braking. CHP added drivers should stay alert for changing road conditions. Courtesy: California Highway Patrol – Santa Cruz. bay area weather 11 hours ago Pacific Ocean Nov 11 Possible thunderstorms Friday afternoon in Bay Area The National Weather Service said there is a chance for thunderstorms Friday afternoon, with the best chance happening north of the Golden Gate.
